_comment: The coverage ratchet read by the 'Coverage must not regress' step in .github/workflows/ci.yml.
It is a FLOOR THAT ONLY MOVES UP, not a target to reach. There is deliberately no minimum:
a fixed threshold rewards tests that touch lines rather than assert behaviour, which is the
exact failure the banned-pattern-3 guard exists to stop (see CLAUDE.md, 'Three banned
patterns'). All this asserts is that a change does not take coverage DOWN.
MEASURED 2026-08-28 on a Windows development host, not on a CI runner: line 85.37, branch
74.17, over the full solution (26 assemblies, 9,737 passed, 12 skipped). The values below are
set a little under those because a runner is not this host - corpus tests skip everywhere, but
SystemFontFact cases depend on which faces are installed. AFTER THE FIRST CI RUN, replace
these with what CI actually reports and delete this paragraph: a baseline carried over from a
developer's machine is the 'unattributable number' benchmarks/README.md warns about, and it is
only here because a CI figure cannot be obtained without a CI run.
The step allows 0.5pp of slack below these values. Raising them is a deliberate act and its
own change - a rise is reported as a notice, never enforced in the PR that caused it, so
adding tests never obliges anyone to also edit this file.
LOWERING them is legitimate exactly once: when the drop is correct, such as dead code being
deleted. Say why in the same commit.

locally as ci.yml runs it (28 assemblies, every one completed), measured line 92.41, branch
